items.title: Candel Therapeutics sinks after prostate-cancer FDA filing pushed into 2027
items.summary: Candel said ongoing FDA discussions and assay refinements now put its prostate-cancer therapy application in mid-2027, versus the prior fourth-quarter 2026 plan. Shares fell sharply after hours despite previously favorable late-stage data. The setback delays the regulatory milestone rather than establishing that the therapy failed; cash runway and FDA requirements are critical.

observations.label: Shares, Nov. 12 after hours (6:24–6:32 PM EST)
observations.value: Dow Jones reported CADL -38% to $5.15 at 6:24 PM; MarketChameleon reported -38.9% at 6:32 PM. Not an official session close.

observations.label: Filing timeline
observations.value: Mid-2027 BLA planned, contingent on ongoing FDA dialogue and assay refinement; previously Q4 2026.

observations.label: Financial capacity
observations.value: Company reported $203.1 million in cash and equivalents as of September 30 and expected operating runway into Q2 2028.

observations.label: Scientific evidence
observations.value: Company cited phase 3 result of 41% lower risk of prostate-cancer recurrence or prostate-cancer-specific death in a specified intermediate-risk subgroup; approval not yet granted.

observations.label: Next indicators / invalidation
observations.value: FDA agreement on assay and BLA requirements, revised filing milestones, cash burn, funding needs, confirmatory efficacy and safety data.

items.key_finding: A major regulatory-timing setback triggered a roughly 38% after-hours repricing, despite ongoing clinical promise.

items.title: NeuroPace plunges after revenue shortfall and materially reduced full-year outlook
items.summary: NeuroPace cut its 2026 revenue outlook after third-quarter revenue missed estimates amid disruptions at key accounts and field-sales changes. The medical-device company's gross margins improved and its regulatory pipeline progressed, but near-term execution and balance-sheet risks now dominate. Its substantial after-hours drop is a market reaction, not proof the core epilepsy technology failed.

observations.label: Shares, Nov. 12 after hours (6:32 PM EST)
observations.value: MarketChameleon reported NPCE -35.1% to $7.80; StockAnalysis after-hours table showed roughly -33.7%. Changing postmarket indications, not closing prices.

observations.label: Q3 2026 results
observations.value: Revenue $23.1 million versus roughly $27.2 million consensus; total revenue down 1.1% year over year and RNS revenue up 1.4%.

observations.label: 2026 revenue guidance
observations.value: Reduced to $91–92 million from $99.5–101.5 million, roughly 9% lower at midpoint.

observations.label: Financial and clinical context
observations.value: Adjusted gross margin 84.8%; cash/investments/restricted cash $49.5 million and long-term debt $59.2 million as of September 30; FDA submissions and amendments pending.

observations.label: Next indicators / invalidation
observations.value: Recovery in scheduled epilepsy procedures, restoration of major accounts and sales effectiveness, cash flow, FDA review milestones and 2027 sales outlook.

items.key_finding: Revenue guidance deterioration and customer disruptions prompted a roughly one-third after-hours share decline.

items.title: UKMTO confirms November 11 tanker strike and evacuation off UAE Ras Al Khaimah
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 204-26, issued November 12, describes a November 11 projectile strike and engine-room fire on a tanker off Ras Al Khaimah. Reuters identified the vessel as MT Dominica Prosperity and reported all 22 crew safely evacuated. This verifies vessel damage, but not a new Strait closure or a quantified reduction in oil exports.

observations.label: Event date and UKMTO reporting
observations.value: November 11 incident reported in UKMTO Warning 204-26 on November 12; tanker struck about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al Khaimah, UAE

observations.label: Confirmed physical outcome
observations.value: Engine-room fire and 22 crew evacuated safely; Reuters reported vessel MT Dominica Prosperity, Liberia-flagged, operated by Sinokor Maritime; no crew injuries reported

observations.label: Related maritime notices
observations.value: UKMTO also released Warning 203-26 about a separate November 10 tanker strike with casualties, and Update 001 to Warning 202-26; do not count repeated descriptions as additional incidents

observations.label: Energy-market context
observations.value: November 12 Brent $95.82, up about 3.3%, reflects geopolitical repricing alongside diplomatic statements; causal contribution from this individual attack is unquantified

observations.label: Risk and invalidation indicators
observations.value: Watch UKMTO/JMIC updates, fire and hull assessment, tanker movements and port operations, physical crude exports, freight/war-risk premiums, and XLE/XOP relative strength; normal transits and verified no export losses would limit supply effect

items.key_finding: A November 11 Gulf tanker attack is now corroborated as physical vessel damage with crew evacuation, without a verified new oil-flow shutdown.

items.title: Cerebras surges after stronger AI inference cloud earnings and expanded hyperscaler demand
items.summary: Cerebras reported third-quarter core revenue of $230.9 million, up 70%, and raised its 2026 core-revenue outlook to $940 million-$960 million. Independent reports described a roughly 14%-16% after-hours rise after new hyperscaler contracts and strong fourth-quarter guidance. Growth and $26.1 billion of obligations are substantial, but GAAP losses, customer concentration and data-center deployment remain risks.

observations.label: After-hours CBRS observed November 12 at 5:17 PM ET
observations.value: StockTitan reported $111.61 after hours versus $97.75 regular-session close, approximately +14.2%; IBD separately reported a move exceeding 16% at another after-hours observation. Indicative only, not a confirmed after-hours closing price.

observations.label: Third-quarter revenue, reported November 12 after close
observations.value: GAAP $210.8 million (+55% year on year); core non-GAAP $230.9 million (+70%). Cloud services GAAP revenue $141.9 million (+265%). Do not conflate GAAP and core.

observations.label: Guidance and customers
observations.value: Core Q4 revenue $310-$330 million, 47%-49% core gross margin; FY2026 core revenue $940-$960 million. Company reported two new hyperscaler wins; WSJ and IBD separately identify Microsoft among new customers.

observations.label: Fundamentals and downside
observations.value: $26.1 billion remaining performance obligations as of September 30; $7.8 billion cash/restricted cash/short-term investments; GAAP net loss $161.2 million versus $22.2 million year earlier. Hardware revenue declined; backlog concentration remains material.

observations.label: Capacity, next evidence and invalidation
observations.value: 700 MW of data-center capacity under contract for delivery by end-2027, not yet operating. Watch signed customer commitments, actual utilization, 2027 deliveries, GAAP margin and cash use; delayed capacity or weaker contract conversion would undermine outlook.

items.key_finding: Confirmed growth in AI inference-cloud demand is translating into higher Cerebras guidance and an outsized after-hours response, but cash conversion is still unproven.

items.title: Brent rises 3.3% to $95.82 as Iran diplomatic hopes fade despite bearish EIA inventories
items.summary: Brent finished November 12 near $95.82, up 3.3%, and WTI was reported at $88.74, up 2.6%, after President Trump said the United States did not need an Iran deal. The rally overwhelmed a 4.7-million-barrel U.S. crude inventory build. This confirms a market risk-premium repricing, not a newly verified shipping closure.

observations.label: November 12 benchmark close, Brent
observations.value: $95.82 a barrel, +3.3%, independently reported by Associated Press and Wall Street Journal

observations.label: November 12 WTI reported by Wall Street Journal
observations.value: $88.74, +2.6%; second independent closing-price confirmation not obtained for WTI

observations.label: EIA November 12
observations.value: Commercial crude stocks +4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million; inventories roughly 4% below five-year seasonal norm

observations.label: Physical-flow differentiation
observations.value: Previously documented Hormuz tanker attacks persist; no new closing of a route, stoppage of exports or vessel strike independently verified in this pass. MARAD regional advisories 2026-011 and 2026-013 remain active

observations.label: Watch / invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO and MARAD notices, actual vessel transits, Gulf exports, tanker freight, IEA monthly report November 13, Brent-WTI spread and XLE/XOP strength. Credible diplomatic progress would reduce the premium

items.key_finding: Diplomatic-risk repricing outweighed bearish inventories at the oil close, without new proof of reduced physical flows.
